records.region: Northwest Greenland Inland Ice west and southwest of Camp Century, toward Lauge Koch Kyst and the Melville Bugt coastal setting.
records.candidate_name_role: No representative natural-river identity established. Camp Century, Lauge Koch Kyst and Melville Bugt are locality/coastal context labels only.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The original map covers the headward opening, all short ice-interior parts and intermediate bends, the lower ice-margin approach and the actual selected coastal terminal setting. It does not establish one representative named natural river across this modeled sequence.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route opens in Inland Ice, runs north and east, then trends southeast through many small stored parts before bending south toward Lauge Koch Kyst. Its final stored part reaches the generalized ice-margin, exposed-rock and coastal-water belt on the Melville Bugt side. Source contours are glaciological/geological cartography, not evidence that a watercourse follows the entire modeled route.
records.completion_scope: All 67 stored parts of the single selected mainstem, including their intermediate joins, the opening and the final position, were read against contiguous original national-map cartography. There is no substantial unviewed selected interval at ordinary source scale. No exact present ice front, shore vertex, small receiving inlet, glacier identity or hydraulic continuity is claimed.

component_scope_limits: Camp Century is a locality label, Lauge Koch Kyst a coastal regional label, and Melville Bugt a coastal-water label. None names the whole selected river group.
Inland Ice terrain correspondence does not prove a surface or subglacial river, a surveyed drainage route or natural-river continuity.
The legend identifies surface contours, ice-thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments; these are not a surveyed river network.
The 1995 national map supports generalized historical terrain and terminal geography, not exact current shore/ice position or an ordinary river-mouth location.
A null candidate means this source pass did not establish the name; it does not assert that no local or official name exists.

records.candidate_name_role: Bounded receiving-river/system candidate supported across the selected East Fork approach and the main Chehalis corridor to Aberdeen. The actual final southwestward segment and inland endpoint are not established as part of that waterway, so this is not a completed whole-selection representative identity.
records.material_pending_reason: Ordinary primary geographic evidence that the actual selected southwestward terminal segment and its endpoint form a through-waterway connection with the mapped Chehalis River. The inspected original instead maps intervening South Aberdeen land and streets.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected opening corresponds to East Fork Chehalis River north of Elochoman Pass, then the Chehalis receiving corridor through Chehalis–Centralia, Oakville, Elma and Montesano to Aberdeen. Both inter-fragment transitions are supported. The final selected southwestward segment instead crosses the South Aberdeen landward street setting and has no established waterway connection.
records.completion_scope: A bounded original-source pass inspected all three selected fragments, the headward opening, mapped forks and major intermediate joins, both fragment transitions and the actual last segment/end. Source geographic coverage was readable throughout, but actual waterway correspondence remains incomplete at the South Aberdeen terminal. One material-pending status is retained.
records.supported_name_scope: East Fork Chehalis River headward selected opening, its mapped union with West Fork, and the Chehalis main corridor through the upper valley, Chehalis–Centralia, Oakville, Elma, Montesano and Aberdeen. Excludes any assertion that the unsupported South Aberdeen terminal segment is a river, that the selected opening is the natural source, or that every reach is named Chehalis River.

component_scope_limits: The actual final selected South Aberdeen waterway link remains unestablished.
The mapped East Fork opening is a selected opening, not a proven natural source.
Chehalis River is a bounded system candidate and does not scalar-name East Fork, West Fork, South Fork, other tributaries, sloughs or lakes.
Formal registry status, historical name equivalence and Korean form were not verified.
Ordinary cartographic generalization and local bend shortcuts are present; no full-geometry, precision, bank, datum or model-error diagnosis was performed.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
